bull.b: Long-term NBM contracts improve revenue visibility, deepen strategic customer relationships and support capacity planning. Their growing share of bits should make the business less dependent on spot NAND pricing, although execution remains important.

The shift toward datacenter, QLC and high-bandwidth products positions SanDisk for structurally rising storage demand from AI and inference. Higher-density, power-efficient technologies can also improve product mix and competitive positioning.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and low leverage
bull.b: Robust cash conversion and minimal leverage provide financial flexibility for technology investment, capacity expansion and shareholder returns. This conservative balance sheet reduces solvency risk during industry downturns, though cash generation remains cycle-sensitive.

bear.b: The recent profit surge demonstrates operating leverage but also highlights exposure to NAND pricing, inventory and demand cycles. If market conditions normalize, margins and cash flow could fall sharply from elevated 2026 levels.

Weak PC and smartphone demand pressures a traditionally important end market and leaves recovery dependent on device replacement cycles. Continued softness could constrain branded and embedded volumes while datacenter growth takes time to offset it.

Allocation constraints may prevent SanDisk from fully capturing demand, while reliance on a small number of major NBM customers increases bargaining and execution risk. A customer-specific delay or contract issue could materially affect results.
